title: The v2 ingest has two behaviours for one input shape and only the destructive one is detectable
body:
MEASURED AND REPORTED BY utilz-vc (Utilz estate, on 8177b53e), filed here by intent-vc because 0090 makes a mis-shaped body permanent. The measurement, the specimen and the repair note are theirs.

A v2 AT row carrying free text where v3 expects a file path is ingested two different ways INSIDE A SINGLE THREAD, FROM A SINGLE MIGRATION, and the branch that produces a clean lint is the honest one.

Specimen: Utilz ST0009, preserved at 3e3bbbe -- `git show 3e3bbbe:intent/.canon/st/ST0009.json`. Nine of thirteen rows took the first branch, three took the second.

BRANCH 1 -- honest, lints clean. No `file` key; the v2 text preserved under `legacy.raw`:

  {"id":"AT-01.1","kind":"test","covers":["AC-01.1"],"status":"green",
   "note":"(red at HEAD: `each_utility: command not found`)",
   "legacy":{"raw":"each_utility() lists installed utilities one per line"}}

The row says, correctly, "I came from v2 and I have no instrument." Nothing is asserted that is not true.

BRANCH 2 -- asserts a path that was never a path, no `legacy` block:

  {"id":"AT-01.2","kind":"test",
   "file":"each_utility() ignores a bin/ symlink that does not resolve to utilz",
   "covers":["AC-01.2"],"status":"green","note":"(red at HEAD)"}

CONSEQUENCES. `intent at lint` reports `AT-01.2 cites a file that does not exist`, and the WP gate goes BLOCKED -- so a thread completed months earlier reads as unfinished work with no explanation the operator can act on. Utilz met it as `ST0009/WP-01 is recorded Done and its gate is BLOCKED` and had no way to know it was an ingest artefact rather than a real contract gap.

WHY THE ASYMMETRY IS THE DEFECT AND NOT THE THREE ROWS. Branch 1's output is complete and truthful and needs no repair. Branch 2's output is a false assertion. Same input class, same run, same thread. And the direction matters: a reader auditing the store sees nine rows that look migrated-and-fine and three that look like someone typed a description into the wrong field, which reads as AUTHOR ERROR rather than TOOL BEHAVIOUR. It took running `intent at lint` and then reading the raw canon side by side to see that the tool did both.

RELATED BUT DISTINCT: 0124 / 0126 / 0129 cover prose-discarded, splice and delimiter injection. This is none of those -- nothing is discarded or corrupted; a value is promoted into the wrong field, and A SIBLING ROW PROVES THE INGEST KNOWS THE RIGHT ONE.

REPAIR, for anyone hitting this: the free text names the test verbatim. In Utilz all three matched `@test` lines in `opt/utilz/test/common_lib.bats` at 402, 411 and 424, so `file` becomes the suite path and the text moves to `note`. `intent at new <ST> <ATID> --covers ... --file ... --status green --note ...` is idempotent on a caller-assigned id and preserves the row's existing status. Utilz repaired ST0009 this way at 2fd5187 and went from 2 doctor findings to 0.

BEARING ON THE UPGRADE PATH, and this is the half that reaches past one estate. The migrator cannot manufacture instrument names v2 never recorded, so every v2 project with free-text ATs inherits a blocked gate on upgrade and hand-repair is the only exit. Three repos met that in one day in three different forms. If that is the intended cost of the upgrade it belongs in the upgrade documentation; if it is not, it is a gap. Either way a consumer meets it as "my closed thread is now blocked and I do not know why".
